links.outcome: Model performance when applied to new population (VHA) beyond development setting
links.effect: AUROC fell from 0.74 to 0.70, subgroup disparities increased, and net-benefit threshold range shifted from [0.1-0.5] to [0.2-0.6].

links.outcome: Effect of development vs local population differences on performance
links.effect: Outcome prevalence rose from 14.65% to 34.34% (P < .001); higher VHA prevalence reduced AUROC and increased subgroup disparities.

links.outcome: Clinical utility via standardized net benefit across subgroups and thresholds
links.effect: Net benefit range shifted from [0.1-0.5] to [0.2-0.6]; opioid-exposed required threshold ~0.5 vs ~0.2 in the general cohort, revealing utility loss not seen in AUROC.
links.quote: For example, opioid-exposed patients required a threshold probability of ∼.5 to achieve net benefit from the model, compared to ∼.2 in the general cohort.

links.outcome: Calibration and subgroup miscalibration in external validation
links.effect: Model overestimates higher probabilities, and underestimates probabilities below 0.6 in opioid-exposed subgroup in Stage 2; depression and opioid-exposed showed most miscalibration.
links.quote: This situation varies in the opioid-exposed subgroup, where the model underestimates probabilities below 0.6 in Stage 2.
